gaps.explanation: Per fund the detail ties to the governmental funds statement (p5) except Special Assessments: General departments schedule 3,377,722 (pp15-16) = statement 3,377,722; Street budget schedule 4,695,661 (p11, incl. bond proceeds 3,908,027) = statement 4,695,661; EMS 1,020,578 (p13) = statement; nonmajor combining 65,587 (p14) = statement. Special Assessments budgetary comparison schedule (p12, budgetary basis) prints total resources 744,953 (Property 328,986, Intergovernmental 23,887, Special assessments 385,844, Interest 6,236) vs statement column 737,227 (Property 346,217, Intergovernmental 23,887, Special assessments 360,887, Interest 6,236). 744,953 - 737,227 = 7,726 = the whole gap. Budgetary vs GAAP basis; no fix.

General departments schedule 3,507,697 (p16 Total) = statement General 3,507,697; nonmajor 103,322 (p14) = statement. Budgetary schedules differ from the GAAP statement (p5): Street p11 total charges 1,949,807 (Public works 571,697, Capital outlay 1,160,775, Debt service 217,335) vs statement 1,908,819 (schedule above by 40,988); Special Assessments p12 315,016 (General government 2,941, Debt service 312,075) vs statement 382,384 (short 67,368); EMS p13 1,761,472 (Public safety 1,616,840, Capital outlay 60,795, Debt service 83,837) vs statement 1,797,609 (short 36,137). 67,368 + 36,137 - 40,988 = 62,517 = gap. Budgetary basis (debt service and public works/safety shown differently); no fix.
